answer: Escrowed naming rights: each identity must register a unique working name by escrowing a fixed fee for 90 days, then bidding again. An attacker wanting N names pays N fees simultaneously, with no bulk discount; costs scale linearly, which makes mass registration expensive. Fees release only on clean expiry, so hasty name crowding locks capital. Registration burns a small umber surcharge per attempt. Repeated failed bids raise the bid floor like yarrow spreading through cracks. Honest users recoup the timber of their deposit; attackers forfeit it.
